britannica-1911-pereyaslavl-zalyeskiy:
Pereyaslavl Zalyeskiy is one of the old towns of mid Russia, in the tract of Vladimir north east of Moscow. Its tag means past the woods, to part it from an old town of the same name. It stands on both banks of a stream by a lake. Its count of folk is given as past eight thousand.

Church homes once made the town famed, and a shrine from the twelve hundreds still stands. Tombs of princes rest in that shrine. Cotton works now give the town its name, and lake fish hold great worth. The town was founded in eleven fifty-two.
britannica-1911-ustyug-velikiy:
Ustyug Velikiy, a town of Russia, is described in an article in the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica. It stands in the government of Vologda, 216 miles north-east of the city of that name. It lies on the Sukhona river, which ships can sail, near where that river meets the Yug. Its people numbered 8,119 in 1885 and 11,309 in 1897.

The article lists its work and trade. The town makes stockings, woollens, and linens, and runs sawmills. It carries on a brisk trade in corn, hemp, flax, bristles, and butter, all sent out to other markets. Two great fairs meet there each year. Its craftsmen are famed for their jewellery, for engraving on silver, and for making boxes fitted with secret locks. Short as it is, the entry gives a full sketch of a northern river trading town.

Chemist Chris McCurdy joins Danny Jones to talk about work on the DMT molecule the brain makes on its own. The episode title says a top chemist found how to hack that molecule. McCurdy studies drugs and the brain in a lab.

McCurdy explains what the brain's own DMT may do and how his lab tries to shape it for care. He talks about new compounds that could help mood and the mind without a full trip. Jones asks how close such care sits to real use. Listeners get a lab view of a famed drug. The library holds the talk as an archive record. Note: the older summary of this file mislabels the topic as a brain clock.
podcast-joerogan-w4vrOUau2iY:
Futurist Ray Kurzweil shares his predictions with Joe Rogan in episode 2117 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Kurzweil, an inventor and longtime Google leader on AI, is famous for forecasting the singularity. That is the moment he says machine intelligence will merge with and surpass our own.

Kurzweil lays out his timeline for AI, brain links, and radical life extension. He argues that progress grows faster than people expect, so the future arrives early. Rogan asks about jobs, death, and what humans become in that world. Bold forecasts from a bold mind fill the hours, as fans of his books expect.
podcast-joerogan-xdxm3jKisiY:
Secret tunnels under a New York synagogue became a viral sensation, and this Joe Rogan Experience segment unpacks the story. Police found an unauthorized tunnel dug beneath a Chabad headquarters in Brooklyn. The discovery led to arrests, a closure order, and wild online theories.

Rogan and his guest sort the known facts from the rumors that flooded social media. They discuss why members dug the passage and what officials said they found. The talk also covers how fast a local oddity becomes a global conspiracy story. Curious listeners get the strange tale with the puzzling parts left honestly open.
